REPORT PROFILE
Format: Old Indian GAAP (Companies Act 1956, old Schedule VI) - standalone accounts only
Year ended: 30 September 1977 (check the notes for the length of the previous period)
Currency/units: Rs. with Indian digit grouping (1,00,000 = 1 lakh; 1,00,00,000 = 1 crore)
Statements in this report: Profit and Loss Account, Balance Sheet
Statements NOT in this report: Cash Flow Statement, Statement of Changes in Equity (not required at the time)
Source quality: may be re-typed from the printed report; figures may contain transcription errors

Annual report: Reliance-1976-1977.pdf
Statements: Manually selected pages
Notes provided: PDF pages 13
Primary financial statements provided: Profit & Loss Account for the Year Ended 30th September, 1977 (PDF p.14); Balance Sheet as at 30th September, 1977 (PDF p.13)

QUESTION: What is on these pages?

Structure your answer as:
## Summary
3–5 bullet points with the key conclusions.
## Key figures
A table with columns: Item | Current year | Prior year | Change | % change | Source.
## Detailed analysis
Trends, drivers, ratios and interpretation relevant to the question.
## Impact on the financial statements
How the matters in the notes flow into and affect each primary statement. Use one sub-heading per statement:
### Profit and Loss Account
### Balance Sheet
(This report has no Cash Flow Statement. If cash movements matter to the question, add a short derived funds-flow statement, clearly labelled as derived by the analyst and not published.)
For each one, name the line items affected, give their figures (current and prior year, citing statement and page), show how the note reconciles to them, and explain the effect. For example, how the tax expense in the note drives profit after tax, how deferred tax balances appear on the Balance Sheet, how taxes paid appear in operating cash flow, or how OCI items move reserves in equity.
## Red flags & areas for follow-up
Anything unusual, inconsistent, or worth asking management about, including any note figure that does not agree with the statements.
## Sources
The notes, statements and PDF pages you relied on.
